sections.html:
Jasper is small and rural. Monticello is the only city and the county seat, and Shady Dale is the one town. The county covers 373 square miles. Public education is a four-school system that includes Jasper County High School.

Population is 17,632 as of mid-2025, up 20.8% from the 2020 count, where the prior decade added only 4.9%. Anyone buying acreage is likely to raise questions on wells, septic and frontage, so have that information ready if you are listing land.

Owners live in 85.6% of occupied homes. For 2020 to 2024 the typical owned home is valued at $243,400, typical rent is $970 a month and middle household income is $60,134. The county has 7,118 housing units, and 124 permits were issued in 2025.

Monthly owner costs are $1,461 with a mortgage and $480 without. The average commute is 39.2 minutes, a long drive that reflects the pull of the Atlanta metro area. Of 6,270 housing units in 2020, 13.7% stood vacant. Those carrying costs help when you test an asking price against the $243,400 middle value.

sections.h2: Which office answers which tax question
sections.html:
A bill passes through several hands, and the Tax Commissioner's are the last. Millage comes from the commission and school board, value from the assessors, dispute rulings from a board the Grand Jury appoints, and mailing and collecting from the commissioner.

  • Tax Commissioner: 126 W. Greene Street, Suite 125, Monticello, GA 31064; (706) 468-4902; counter open Monday through Friday, 8 to 4:30.
  • Tax Assessor: signs off on exemptions and notifies owners when it changes a value.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: the courthouse deed room provides warranty deed copies.

One mill is a dollar per thousand of assessed value, and 40% of market value is the assessed figure.

sections.h2: When a Jasper County bill comes due
sections.html:
On the standing schedule, land, buildings and business personal property are paid in two halves, September 20 and December 20. Statewide, December 20 is the standard deadline, and interest holds off until two months after the bill is postmarked.

The 2026 notice departed from that schedule: mailing on October 16, a first installment dated November 20, and the balance dated December 20. Printed dates can differ from year to year, so the ones on your own statement win.

  • Manufactured housing: payment and a location permit by April 1 each year.
  • Missing it brings a 10% penalty and possibly a citation to Magistrate Court or sale of the unit.
  • Vehicles renew during the 30 days that end on the owner's birthday.

A lien often surfaces just as a sale nears closing. Taxes left unpaid past 90 days are recorded as a tax FiFa with the Clerk of Superior Court, and the county warns that property can be levied on and sold.

Anyone can read a FiFa entry, credit bureaus included, and the tax office cannot dictate how they use it. Clear a recorded lien before closing.

The balance is available at (706) 468-4902. If your closing falls between the two installment dates, settle who pays each half and put that in the settlement papers.

  1. Call the commissioner for the current balance and any earlier years.
  2. Ask the Clerk of Superior Court whether a FiFa has been recorded against the parcel.
  3. Decide who pays each installment and write it into the settlement papers.
  4. Bring a copy of your deed, available from the courthouse deed room, if the title has any gaps.

A cash sale skips the lender's underwriting, which leaves tax payoff and lien release as the main items before the deed changes hands.

The base exemption is two thousand dollars off assessed value. It reduces the county, school and State levies, but the share of the rate that retires bonds is excluded.

Apply at the Tax Commissioner's counter with a driver's license that shows your Jasper County address. A form received by April 1 counts for that year. Approval carries over each year until you move, change owners or switch type, and a bigger local exemption replaces the State figure.

sections.h2: How to dispute a Jasper County value
sections.html:
You have 45 days counting from the notice date. Pick the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator. Either outcome can go to Superior Court once you send written notice to the Board of Tax Assessors.

Prepare ahead. During the January 1 to April 1 return period an owner can state a personal view of market value, which creates solid ground if the assessors alter it. Mobile home owners have 45 days to file with the assessors and 21 days after a change notice to reach the Board of Equalization.

Tax assessed or collected in error or illegally can be recovered through a written request filed within three years of paying. When the claim comes from an appealed value, the refund is processed once the final taxable value is fixed.

City tax is a separate levy. Municipalities tax on their own, and the city clerk sends and collects that bill unless city and county have agreed on one combined bill. Vehicle tax is always collected by the county Tax Commissioner.

Holders of long-term notes secured by real estate must record them within 90 days, at the intangible recording rate of $1.50 per $500 of face amount or part of it.

Returns for taxable property are accepted January 1 through April 1. An owner who files none is treated as repeating last year's value and last year's real property exemptions.

Mail goes to the last address the county has, so report any move. Three programs change how land or buildings are valued.

  • Historic property: a building on the Georgia register, with up to two acres around it, may be assessed preferentially.
  • Brownfield sites: land approved for cleanup can keep a frozen value for a decade.
  • Public safety survivors: the unremarried spouse of a firefighter or officer killed on duty may be fully exempt once the agency's papers are filed.

If your property is in a program, the Board of Tax Assessors can say what a buyer must do to keep the status.

faqs.q: What is the street address for the Jasper County tax counter?
faqs.a: 126 W. Greene Street, Suite 125, Monticello, GA 31064, telephone (706) 468-4902. Weekday hours run 8 to 4:30.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for a first Jasper County homestead claim?
faqs.a: April 1 of the first year. Anything later counts toward the next tax year, and the home must have been yours and lived in on January 1.

faqs.q: Does a Jasper County tax lien reach my credit file?
faqs.a: Possibly. Ninety days past due puts a FiFa lien on record with the Clerk of Superior Court, and those entries are public.

faqs.q: How do I get a Jasper County deed copy?
faqs.a: Visit the deed room of the Clerk of Superior Court in the Jasper County Courthouse.

faqs.q: What is the Jasper County appeal deadline?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the date printed on the assessment notice. A later written notice to the Board of Tax Assessors carries a ruling to Superior Court.
